title: Teneggi 2013 social modulation face PPS
citation: Teneggi, C., Canzoneri, E., di Pellegrino, G., & Serino, A. (2013). Social modulation of peripersonal space boundaries. Current Biology, 23(5), 406-411.
notes: Experiment 1 schedule for one social condition. Run it separately for the mannequin and unfamiliar-person conditions and counterbalance their order between participants. The preview uses generated audio and toolkit response and tactile proxies. The publication's equipment and calibrations are recorded as reference values.

implemented_controls: auditory-only catch trials with response withholding

experiment_1.instructions: Maintain gaze on the face of the mannequin or unfamiliar person during the assessment.
experiment_1.condition_order: Counterbalanced between participants. Complete both blocks of one condition before changing the setting.
experiment_1.randomization: Targets and catches were randomly intermingled. The original randomization algorithm, seed, catch split by direction and per-block trial-type composition are unreported.

trial_timing.distance_definition: D1 is farthest and D5 is closest. These are ordered perceptual bins. The study does not give metric coordinates for the five bins.

published_apparatus.sound: Two hidden same-height loudspeakers beside the seated participant, with the near speaker about 5 cm from the right cheek and the other about 100 cm from the near speaker. Both played the same 44.1 kHz pink-noise sample simultaneously with opposing channel gains.
published_apparatus.sound_envelope: Exponential rise for IN and exponential fall for OUT. Near and far gain directions were reversed for OUT.
published_apparatus.tactile: Digitimer DS7A constant-current stimulator and Ambu Neuroline electrode pair on the right cheek. One rectangular monophasic pulse with a reported duration of 100 microseconds.
published_apparatus.tactile_calibration: Individual suprathreshold setting. Verify all 10 stimuli among 5 catches and repeat with a 5 mA increase if any response is missed or given on a catch. The original study reports observed settings of 60–90 mA.
published_apparatus.response: Say TAH as quickly as possible after touch. The original used a voice-activated relay. RT was computed as the vocal timestamp minus the scheduled tactile-onset timestamp, both measured from trial start.

experiment_2.schedule: The same audio-tactile timing and count per assessment as Experiment 1. Assess the participant with the same confederate before and after a one-shot bargaining game.
experiment_2.assignment: Cooperative versus non-cooperative confederate behavior was assigned between participants, 16 in each group. The two confederates were counterbalanced across roles.
experiment_2.profile_scope: The bargaining game and between-participant assignment require a separate procedure.

experiment_3.schedule: IN only, 2000 mm loudspeaker separation, 4000 ms sound, 500 ms silence before and after. Tactile onsets were 250, 750, 1300, 1800, 2500, 3200, and 3700 ms after sound onset.
experiment_3.profile_scope: Requires its own trial profile. Per-assessment target repetitions and catch allocation are unreported for this variant.

implementation_gaps: Exact original pink-noise source and two loudspeaker gain functions are unavailable.
Exact physical response capture requires the original voice-key threshold, recording latency calibration and response cutoff.
Exact apparatus-specific tactile delivery requires a calibrated physical stimulator and timing verification.
Other-person/mannequin context must be arranged and counterbalanced by the operator.
Economic-game manipulation is a separate procedure in Experiment 2.

provenance.source: Current Biology version of record pp. 406–407, Experiment 1 and Figure 1. Supplemental Experimental Procedures pp. 7 and 9–10, Participants and Social Interactions.

provenance.field: Stimulus, timing, trial allocation and response
provenance.source: Supplemental Experimental Procedures pp. 7–9, Apparatus and Stimuli, Design and Procedure, and Data Analysis and Sigmoid Fitting.
Current Biology version of record pp. 407–409 and Supplemental Experimental Procedures pp. 7 and 9–11. The shared Experiment 2 assessment and alternate Experiment 3 timings are documented separately.

The toolkit uses a generated continuous pink-noise source and a virtual path with nominal endpoints about 105 and 5 cm to define a three-second preview. These are renderer settings only. The toolkit seed and block allocation are reproducibility defaults.
